hook.line: When something feels off and you have no proof, you need words that are softer than an accusation. These give you a hunch, and one of them also warns of bad news.
hook.es: Me da la sensación de que nos está escondiendo algo.
hook.en: I get the feeling he's hiding something from us.

examples.es: Me da la sensación de que nos está escondiendo algo.
examples.en: I get the feeling he's hiding something from us.

examples.es: Tengo la sospecha de que ya lo sabe.
examples.en: I have a suspicion she already knows.

examples.es: Me temo que no va a llegar.
examples.en: I'm afraid he isn't going to make it.

examples.es: Tengo la impresión de que nadie dice la verdad.
examples.en: I have the impression nobody is telling the truth.

examples.es: Me da la sensación de que Tomás no quiere hablar.
examples.en: I get the feeling Tomás doesn't want to talk.

examples.es: ¿Tienes la sensación de que algo cambió?
examples.en: Do you have the feeling something changed? (to a friend)

rule:
These openers all say "I think so, but I can't prove it":

*Me da la sensación de que...* (I get the feeling)
*Tengo la sospecha de que...* (I have a suspicion)
*Tengo la impresión de que...* (I have the impression)
*Me temo que...* (I'm afraid that), for unwelcome news

After them comes a normal sentence with a plain verb: *está escondiendo*, *no va a llegar*.

Watch *de*: it is *de que* after the nouns, but *me temo que* has none.
smallPrint: Teachers call these verbs and phrases of opinion and suspicion. They take the plain indicative, because the speaker believes what follows.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que el café va a cerrar.
options: I'm afraid the café is going to close.
I hope the café is going to close.
The café closed.

readAndPick.es: Me da la sensación de que ya lo sabías.
options: I get the feeling I already knew.
You get the feeling I already knew.
I get the feeling you already knew.

readAndPick.es: Tengo la sospecha de que Altamira tiene prisa.
options: I have a suspicion Altamira is in a hurry.
I have a suspicion Altamira was in a hurry.
Altamira has a suspicion I am in a hurry.
I'm afraid it's too early.
I'm afraid it's late.
I'm afraid it was late.

readAndPick.es: Tenemos la impresión de que nadie dice la verdad.
options: We have the impression nobody is telling the truth.
I have the impression nobody is telling the truth.
We have the impression everybody is telling the truth.

readAndPick.es: ¿Tienes la sensación de que algo cambió?
options: Do I have the feeling something changed?
Do you have the feeling something changed?
Did you have the feeling nothing changed?

readAndPick.es: Me da la sensación de que Tomás no quiere hablar.
options: I get the feeling Tomás wants to talk.
I get the feeling Tomás can't talk.
I get the feeling Tomás doesn't want to talk.

readAndPick.es: Me temo que no va a llegar.
options: I'm afraid he isn't going to make it.
I'm afraid he is going to make it.
I hope he isn't going to make it.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *que* or *de que* and type the whole sentence: *Me temo ___ no va a llegar.*
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que no va a llegar.
yourTurn.why: *Me temo* goes straight into *que*, with no *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I get the feeling Tomás doesn't want to talk.
yourTurn.answer: Me da la sensación de que Tomás no quiere hablar.
accept: Tengo la sensación de que Tomás no quiere hablar.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I have a suspicion Altamira is in a hurry.
yourTurn.answer: Tengo la sospecha de que Altamira tiene prisa.
yourTurn.why: *Tengo la sospecha de que* then a normal sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm afraid the café is going to close.
yourTurn.answer: Me temo que el café va a cerrar.
yourTurn.why: *Me temo que* also hints that the news is unwelcome.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: Do you have the feeling something changed?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Tienes la sensación de que algo cambió?

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *we*: We have the impression nobody is telling the truth.
yourTurn.answer: Tenemos la impresión de que nadie dice la verdad.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I'm afraid it's late.

pitfalls.wrong: Me temo de que no va a llegar.
pitfalls.right: Me temo que no va a llegar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. With *me temo*, go straight to *que*; the *de* belongs to the nouns like *sensación*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me da la sensación de que nos esté escondiendo algo.
pitfalls.right: Me da la sensación de que nos está escondiendo algo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You believe it, so the verb stays plain: *está*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tengo miedo que no va a llegar.
pitfalls.right: Me temo que no va a llegar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Tengo miedo* is real fear; "I'm afraid that" in the polite sense is *me temo que*.

personal: Tell a friend a hunch about your week with *Me da la sensación de que* or *Me temo que*.
